claims.statement: The Texas Homeowners Appetite Guide is internal underwriting guidance rather than policy contract language; the enterprise referral matrix permits state guides to impose tighter authority but not broader authority, and a referral cannot approve a filing or bulletin violation.

Texas base appetite is owner-occupied one-family primary residences with Coverage A from $150,000 through $1,200,000, insurance of at least 80% of replacement cost, frame/masonry/masonry-veneer construction, and protection class 1-8; seasonal and secondary residences are permitted only in protection classes 1-6 with a five-year clear prior-loss record.

Texas applies a tighter state-specific Coverage A authority model: line underwriters may bind through $800,000, senior underwriters through $1,200,000 and one referral condition, and Coverage A above $1,200,000 or more than one referral condition requires management approval.

For Texas new business and renewal, roof surfacing aged 15 years or more requires HO 23 74; roof surfacing aged 25 years or more is outside appetite regardless of endorsement unless a full roof replacement is documented within 90 days of binding.

The enterprise matrix requires referral for roof surfacing age 20 years or more, which adds escalation to Texas's 15-year roof-schedule control but does not replace Texas's stricter 25-year eligibility rule.

Texas treats 14 enumerated counties as coastal for its operational roof and wind/hail controls, and requires a composition-shingle roof in those counties to have an inspection report dated within 12 months of the effective date; this operational list is distinct from the form and bulletin seacoast-territory definitions.

Bulletin B-2021-08 applies to Texas residential property policies delivered or issued for delivery with effective dates on or after 2022-01-01; HO 01 45 is effective on the same policy-effective-date threshold, attaches to HO-3, and controls a conflict only when attached.

Texas wind/hail deductible configuration is constrained by B-2021-08: percentage deductibles may be 1%-5% of Coverage A, with a 10% seacoast maximum, and a flat dollar deductible may not be below the all-other-perils deductible; the amendment and rate rule must be filed and approved or deemed approved before application, and Declarations disclosure plus 30-day renewal-increase notice are required.

For an issued applicable HO 01 45 policy, a windstorm-or-hail loss uses only the separate wind/hail deductible; mixed covered-peril damage uses separate deductibles when attributable portions can be determined and otherwise only the larger deductible applies.

Texas's residual-market wind/hail exclusion route requires referral and a signed acknowledgment at binding; under HO 01 45, the policy result additionally depends on Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage and an attached exclusion endorsement, and T.1 does not apply when wind/hail is excluded this way.

Texas permits up to $25,000 of HO 04 90 water-backup limit without referral only when there has been no water-backup claim in five years; two or more such claims in five years makes the endorsement outside appetite while allowing the underlying policy without it, and a finished below-grade basement needs a battery-backed sump pump for a limit over $10,000.

A water-backup request above $25,000 is a matrix referral and enterprise senior authority reaches $50,000, subject to Texas's separate claim, sump, and one-referral senior controls; the matrix independently makes three or more paid water claims of any type in five years a non-clearable entire-risk hard stop.

HO 04 90 default payment terms depend on the selected edition: 2010-10 provides a $5,000 per-policy-period sublimit within the applicable A/B/C limits and a separate $500 deductible, while 2026-01 provides a $10,000 sublimit and a separate $1,000 deductible; in either edition, W.3 displaces the Section I Declarations deductible for covered endorsement loss.

Texas requires senior referral for two or more paid property claims in three years and for any mold, continuous-seepage, or foundation-movement claim; a prior liability claim involving a dog bite, trampoline, or unfenced pool also requires referral and a completed liability supplement.
Every cleared referral must document the condition, clearing authority level, specific facts relied on, and date; without the recorded basis it is treated as unbound authority in audit.

For an issued, attached, and applicable HO 01 45 endorsement, T.1 implements Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 and amends HO-3 2018-09 S.5 so a windstorm-or-hail loss receives only the separate windstorm/hail deductible rather than the all-other-perils deductible.

The Texas residual-market wind/hail exclusion route has distinct controls: G.4 requires a signed acknowledgment at binding for the operational seacoast/residual-market path, matrix R.3 requires referral, and issued-form T.7 additionally requires Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage and attachment of the applicable exclusion endorsement before T.1 does not apply.

For an issued compatible HO-3 policy with HO 04 90 edition 2010-10, 2026-01, or 2027-01 attached, W.1 supplies the limited direct-physical-loss write-back for the Section I A.3 sewer/drain-backup and sump-event category, while W.4 preserves the A.1 flood/surface-water and A.2 subsurface-water exclusions; Texas G.3 binding thresholds remain separate underwriting constraints.

For a verified attached HO 04 90, 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it; 2026-01 replaced it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01 and remains in force for policies written under it; and 2027-01 replaces 2026-01 for policies written on or after 2027-01-01. Attachment, exact endorsement edition, policy-written date, and endorsement Declarations must be established before stating edition-specific contract terms.

Only HO 04 90 2026-01 adds a finished-below-grade coverage condition: at the time of loss, an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent backflow-prevention device must serve the sewer line; that condition does not appear in 2010-10.

For HO 04 90 water-backup loss, 2010-10 W.6 and 2026-01 W.7 each leave Coverage A/B settlement on the attached policy basis and settle Coverage C at actual cash value unless the endorsement Declarations state otherwise.

Texas G.3's $5,000 HO 04 90 base-sublimit reference matches the 2010-10 default but conflicts with the $10,000 default in 2026-01; the supplied guide and referral matrix do not provide a resolution or amend the selected issued endorsement terms.

Texas G.3's battery-backed-sump requirement is a pre-bind control only for a finished basement below grade and a requested limit above $10,000, while 2026-01 W.6 is an at-loss serving-sewer backflow-device condition for any finished-below-grade residence; neither test substitutes for the other and W.6 does not apply to 2010-10.

Both HO 04 90 editions withhold endorsement coverage when the backup, overflow, or discharge resulted from the insured's known pre-loss failure to maintain the serving sewer line, drain, sump, or sump pump and a reasonable person would have remedied it.

HO 04 90 edition 2027-01 carries forward the 2026-01 edition's $10,000 per-policy-period default sublimit unless a higher limit appears in the endorsement Declarations, separate $1,000 deductible, finished-below-grade installed-and-operable backflow-prevention condition, and W.7 settlement provisions; these terms differ from 2010-10 and apply only after the attached edition is verified.
